pages.text: A bookshelf that never learned to read. Quanta 85 says it doesn't need to.

pages.title: Shelf Math
pages.text: Set OreSpawn storage blocks around an Apothic enchanting table like bookshelves and they read as stats:$(p)$(thing)Uranium$() — Quanta +85, Eterna -10.$(br)$(thing)Ruby$() — Eterna +5 (cap 75), Arcana +17.5.$(br)$(thing)Tiger's Eye$() — Eterna +15 (cap 90), one extra clue.$(br)$(thing)Titanium$() — Eterna +6 (cap 60), Quanta -3, Arcana +2.

pages.title: Volatile, On Purpose
pages.text: One uranium block covers the entire Quanta bill of every recipe in this book — the table gets volatile, you get options. High Quanta means wilder swings on what the table offers; when it gets too creative, titanium is your calming agent.$(p)Shelving your first uranium block signs the $(thing)Breeder Corner$() advancement. The librarian moved out. The physicist moved in.

pages.title: The Infusion
pages.text: Build the table to $(thing)Eterna 60, Quanta 85, Arcana 25$(), then enchant a plain uranium ingot like any other item. The altar infuses it into a $(thing)Radioactive II$() book: strikes poison the target. Perfectly safe for the wielder. Notably less so for everyone else.

pages.title: Radioactive, the Enchant
pages.text: Off the table itself, Radioactive rolls up to level III and sits on swords and the mace alike — the poison runs longer and meaner with every level. The full write-up lives with the other $(l:orespawn_integrations:modern_wonders/new_enchantments)New Enchantments$(), next to its cold-blooded sibling, Kraken's Grip.
